Time adds up each call's own length. Calls in a thread can overlap; counted
once, they come to 25h on the clock. Recap's 'tools' hours are counted another
way.
5 calls were marked finished all at once, though they started at different
times, most likely when a run stopped. When each really finished is not known,
so their time is not counted and they are not among the longest: totals of
time can only be too small. 2 more calls never ended and add no time.
A line like "cd app && cargo test | tail" is one call, named for its main
program, cargo: its time, failure and exit code are the whole line's. 56% of
command lines ran two or more programs on the list. Programs are named from a
list of 75 common ones; a command with none of them is "not on the list".
Only program and tool names and exit codes are read. Numbers may be cached in
your cache folder; nothing is sent.
